newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB futures sharply lower on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB futures sharply lower on long liquidation.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Thursday's Tokyo session sharply lower.
The December closed down 0.50 at the day's low of 124.35, on liquidation of long positions, traders said.
It opened at the day's high of 125.05 on news that the Ministry of Finance had suspended most business operations of Hanwa Bank Ltd, a regional bank in western Japan.
But JGB futures quickly turned lower on speculative selling by foreign players, remaining in negative territory for most of the day, traders said.

News of trouble in the banking industry is normally considered as a bullish factor for JGBs, as it underscores the need for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to maintain an easy monetary policy to help financial institutions cope with problem loans.

"Some dealers were liquidating long positions towards the end of the session. However, investors were not very active and no major activities were detected in cash JGBs," said a trader at a trust bank's securities unit.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.660 percent as of 3.20 p.m.(0620 GMT), up from 2.610 percent on Wednesday.
There was some relief in the JGB market when the Land Policy Council's proposals, released in late morning, failed to boost stock prices.
Earlier in the day, some had feared that a drastic review of land taxes would be bullish for stocks but bearish for bonds. The proposals did not contain such measures.
Market players were cautious ahead of the release of the BOJ's key quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment on November 27.
Experts generally expect the tankan to show only a mild improvement in business confidence.
"Even if the tankan turns out to be stronger than expected, the downside is likely to be limited, as investors are keen to buy on dips," a trader at a brokerage house said.
Japan Airlines Co Ltd launched a 30 billion yen 10-year straight bond with a coupon of 2.90 percent on Thursday.

As the 10-year straight bond with a coupon of 2.95 percent recently issued by Odakyu Electric Railway was still facing selling pressure, it may be difficult to attract buyers to the JAL bond, some traders said.
